name: Devin
verdict: No OAuth: each customer org admin creates a service user with a least-privilege role and sends you the key and org ID. On enterprise accounts an admin policy can disable keys; about 1-3 days.
needGuide: No — just collect a service-user key and org ID (Settings → Devin API → Service users).

auth.detail: Devin API v3 uses Bearer tokens only, prefixed `cog_`: service user API keys (RBAC) and personal access tokens (PATs). Legacy v1/v2 keys (`apk_`, `apk_user_`) are deprecated. The MCP server (https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp, Streamable HTTP) takes a `cog_` key as a bearer token; no OAuth is documented anywhere. Enterprise service-user keys and PATs also need an X-Org-Id header.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review); depends on customer admin

approval.gate: No OAuth app review. Each customer creates their own service-user key and pastes it into your app. The Enterprise API (/v3/enterprise/*) is for enterprise customers only, and on enterprise accounts PATs are disabled by default behind an admin policy that can require approval and expiry.

scopes.why: RBAC roles on the service user rather than OAuth scopes.
scopes.summary: RBAC roles on the service user rather than OAuth scopes. Organization API (/v3/organizations/*) covers sessions, knowledge, playbooks and secrets. Enterprise API (/v3/enterprise/*) covers analytics, audit logs, users and billing. Impersonation needs ImpersonateOrgSessions.

cost: Requires a Devin account (Teams or Enterprise plan for service users, likely); API usage consumes the customer's Devin quota
prerequisites: Account and owner: A Devin org admin on your side who can create service users; the page does not state which roles can provision them.
Where you register: Org: Settings → Devin API → Service users tab. Enterprise: Enterprise settings → Devin API → Service users. Assign a role, copy the cog_ key (shown once).
Cost: Requires a Devin account (Teams or Enterprise plan for service users, likely); API usage consumes the customer's Devin quota

registerAt.path: Org: Settings → Devin API → Service users tab. Enterprise: Enterprise settings → Devin API → Service users. Assign a role, copy the cog_ key (shown once).

steps.do: In your Devin org go to Settings → Devin API → Service users and create a service user with a least-privilege role.
Copy the cog_ key once and store it in a secrets manager.
Call GET /v3/self on api.devin.ai with `Authorization: Bearer cog_...` to verify.
Create sessions through /v3/organizations/{org}/sessions; use create_as_user_id if the role has ImpersonateOrgSessions.
Build a customer-facing setup screen that asks for the key and org ID, stores them encrypted, validates with /v3/self and shows the minimum role needed.
Optionally configure the Devin MCP server with the key and X-Org-Id header for enterprise keys.

roles.team: A Devin org admin on your side who can create service users; the page does not state which roles can provision them.
roles.console: Custom roles and RBAC (enterprise): assign a role to the service user in the Devin API tab; the role limits which endpoints it can call.
roles.customer: A customer org or enterprise admin creates a service user with a least-privilege role, and sends you the key and org ID. Enterprise admins can disable PATs and enforce SSO/IP allowlists.

testing: Use your own Devin org and a test service user.
Rate limits were not found in the docs.

blockers.problem: No OAuth, so users must paste keys
blockers.fix: Key-entry UI with validation and rotation guidance.

blockers.problem: Legacy apk_ keys do not work with most MCP tools
Enterprise PATs are disabled by default
blockers.fix: Use service users, or ask the admin to change the policy.

blockers.problem: Enterprise service-user key creation endpoints are Beta

automation.agentCan: Write the key-validation and session-creation client, configure MCP, draft the customer setup guide and role recommendations, and run test sessions.
automation.humanMust: A Devin admin logs in to create service users and keys, pays for the plan, and approves enterprise policies.

uncertain: Which roles may create service users, rate limits, the exact plan needed for service users, and any OAuth roadmap were not documented.
